# python-prompt-toolkit: diagnosing widespread input, suggestion and rendering misbehaviour without a test suite

A program that takes keystrokes at an interactive prompt, offers the user candidates as they type, and paints decorated text back to the terminal now behaves wrongly in a great many everyday situations, in ways that look unrelated to each other. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Everything below is what I could observe from the outside, without reading the source.

Moving around while typing. With the default chord set, moving the cursor forward over a run of letters (control-right, or Esc then f) lands it one character away from where that run really begins, so a character inserted after such a move ends up inside the neighbouring run instead of at its edge. Positive repeat counts still behave: Esc 4 x inserts four x's, and Esc 4 4 x inserts forty-four. The negative prefix, though, is dead. Esc minus followed by the right arrow moves forward rather than backward, and repeating the minus, or typing it before a digit count and then a movement or a line kill, is treated as if no sign had been given; there seem to be two distinct problems with that prefix, one when the minus is the first thing typed after Esc and another in the check for whether a count is already pending.
